question: Zelená pasta wasabi, ktorú dostanete k sushi v bežnom obchode, väčšinou vôbec nie je pravé wasabi. Na akej koreninovej zelenine je naozaj založená? Slováci ju poznajú najmä z Veľkej noci k šunke.
source_excerpt: a blend of common horseradish, mustard flour, and green food coloring

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the green paste in a supermarket sushi box is an exotic Japanese plant; it turns out to be the same root Slovaks grate onto Easter ham. The Easter-ham foothold makes it reasonable to work out.
extra.verification_notes: Imitation wasabi paste is mainly horseradish (chren) with mustard and green dye; sources agree, e.g. https://www.chowhound.com/2262138/is-japanese-and-american-wasabi-different/

explanation: Pravé wasabi je drahé a po nastrúhaní stratí chuť za pár minút, preto sa namiesto neho používa chren s horčicou a zeleným farbivom. K sushi teda často jete to isté, čo máte na Veľkú noc k šunke, len zafarbené nazeleno.

question: Dobrá správa pre každého, komu z paličiek padá sushi: nigiri sa podľa japonskej etikety pokojne smie jesť aj bez nich. Čím teda?
source_excerpt: it's only sashimi that absolutely must be picked with chopsticks

extra.why_interesting: Many people struggling with chopsticks assume using them is the polite 'rule'. In fact, eating nigiri by hand is fully proper in Japan. Players can reason toward it because there is only one obvious alternative to chopsticks.
extra.verification_notes: Etiquette sources agree nigiri may properly be eaten by hand rather than with chopsticks; only sashimi strictly requires chopsticks (https://www.foodrepublic.com/1459258/sushi-chopstick-etiquette-nigiri-sashimi).

explanation: Sushi vzniklo ako rýchle jedlo z pouličných stánkov a nigiri sa v Japonsku dodnes bežne je prstami. Kúsok sa do sójovej omáčky namáča rybou, nie ryžou, aby sa nerozpadol.
